title: Embeddings — One Vector Can Hide Several Meanings
key_insight: Contextual embeddings use the surrounding sequence to produce a different vector for each occurrence. Sentence models then pool token information into a search-ready vector.
body:
## One Vector Can Hide Several Meanings

The word “bank” appears in finance and river sentences. A fixed word lookup gives it one vector, but context should change its location.

Contextual embeddings use the surrounding sequence to produce a different vector for each occurrence. Sentence models then pool token information into a search-ready vector.

Test retrieval on real queries. Generic similarity benchmarks can hide failures on names, numbers, negation, or specialized language.
common_mistakes: An embedding is always a readable paragraph.
Vector closeness proves two statements are factually true.
Every similarity metric ranks all vectors identically.

real_world_usage: Embeddings connect text, images, and users to search, recommendation, retrieval, and neural computation.
explain_back_prompt: Using “One Vector Can Hide Several Meanings,” explain Embeddings without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
